title: UK & Scotland Family Trip 2026
subtitle: Scott, Kimberly, Trenton, London + Bella · 11 Days · August 4–14, 2026

days.title: Day 1 — Fly Orlando to London
days.subtitle: August 4, 2026
days.tip: Check in early — international flights recommend arriving 3 hours before departure. Pack carry-on snacks and entertainment for the overnight crossing.

stops.name: Flight Z0 784 — MCO to LGW
stops.notes: Norse Atlantic UK flight Z0 784. Departs Orlando 8:30 PM. Arrives London Gatwick the next morning. Overnight transatlantic flight.

days.title: Day 2 — Arrive London
days.subtitle: August 5, 2026 · British Museum · Patty & Bun · Tower of London
days.tip: After an overnight flight, pace yourselves — skip anything that feels rushed. Westminster Abbey Lates is a quieter evening experience worth saving energy for.

stops.name: Gatwick Express to London Victoria
stops.notes: Gatwick Express runs every 15 minutes, journey ~30 minutes. Buy tickets at the station.

stops.name: Royal Horseguards Hotel — Check In / Drop Bags
stops.notes: 2 Whitehall Court, SW1A 2EJ. Drop bags — rooms may not be ready. Freshen up and head out. [Confirmation PDF kept separately — too large to store in the app.]

stops.name: British Museum
stops.notes: Free entry. Rosetta Stone, Egyptian mummies, Elgin Marbles. Don't try to see everything — hit the highlights. Allow 1.5–2 hours.

stops.name: Patty & Bun — James Street
stops.notes: Iconic cathedral with stunning dome. Climb to the Golden Gallery for panoramic city views. Allow 1–1.5 hours.

stops.name: St. Paul's Cathedral
stops.notes: Iconic cathedral with stunning dome. Climb to the Golden Gallery for panoramic city views. Allow 1–1.5 hours.

stops.name: Tower of London
stops.notes: Crown Jewels, Beefeaters, medieval fortress. Book tickets in advance. Allow 1.5 hours.

stops.name: Westminster Abbey Lates
stops.notes: Special evening opening — quieter crowds than daytime. Book in advance.

stops.name: Dinner — Flat Iron Covent Garden
stops.notes: Affordable quality steak restaurant. Flat Iron cut with a side. No reservations — queue up or arrive at opening.

stops.name: Gelupo Gelato
stops.notes: Legendary Italian gelato in Soho. Perfect nightcap after a long travel day.

days.title: Day 3 — Hampton Court & Windsor
days.subtitle: August 6, 2026 · Hampton Court Palace · Windsor Castle · Tower Bridge
days.tip: Hampton Court and Windsor are both royal palaces on the same rail corridor — a clever double. Book Windsor Castle tickets online to avoid the queue.

stops.name: Hampton Court Palace
stops.notes: Henry VIII's magnificent riverside palace. Great Hall, Tudor kitchens, famous maze. Allow 2–2.5 hours. Book online.

stops.name: Lunch — Tiltyard Cafe
stops.notes: Cafe inside Hampton Court Palace grounds. Convenient for a mid-palace break.

stops.name: Windsor Castle
stops.notes: The oldest and largest occupied castle in the world. State Apartments, St George's Chapel (where royals are buried). Book online. Allow 2 hours.

stops.name: Windsor Town Walk
stops.notes: Explore the charming town below the castle. Good spots for ice cream and window shopping.

stops.name: Rental Car Pick up Waterloo Station
stops.notes: Pick up rental car near hotel. Remember: drive on the left. Sat-nav essential. Car will be ready for an early start tomorrow.

stops.name: Royal Horseguards Hotel
stops.notes: 2 Whitehall Court, SW1A 2EJ.

stops.name: Dinner — Cinnamon Club
stops.notes: 30–32 Great Smith Street, Westminster. Upscale Indian restaurant in a stunning former Victorian library, just a 5-minute walk from the Royal Horseguards Hotel. Reservation recommended.

stops.name: Westminster Evening Walk
stops.notes: Start on Westminster Bridge — great views of Big Ben and the Thames lit up at night. Walk north up Whitehall past the Cenotaph and Horse Guards. End at Trafalgar Square, then loop down The Mall to Buckingham Palace before heading back to the hotel on Whitehall Court.

days.title: Day 4 — London to York via Blenheim
days.subtitle: August 7, 2026 · Blenheim Palace · Woodstock Arms · Lincoln Cathedral
days.tip: Pick up the car early and load bags the night before if possible. Blenheim is best in the morning before coach tours arrive. York Ghost Walk sells out — book online.

stops.name: Blenheim Palace
stops.notes: Churchill's birthplace and one of England's grandest stately homes. UNESCO World Heritage Site. Baroque architecture, formal gardens, grand park. Allow 2 hours.

stops.name: Lunch — Woodstock Arms
stops.notes: Traditional village pub in Woodstock, just outside Blenheim gates. Excellent British pub lunch.

stops.name: Fuel Stop
stops.notes: Fill up before heading through the Cotswolds.

stops.name: Lincoln Cathedral
stops.notes: One of the finest Gothic cathedrals in Europe, and was the world's tallest building for over 200 years. Stunning west front, magnificent interior. Allow 1–1.5 hours. Book tickets online.

stops.name: Lincoln Castle
stops.notes: Norman castle built by William the Conqueror. Houses one of only four surviving original Magna Carta documents. Walk the medieval walls for great views over the city and cathedral. Allow 1 hour.

stops.name: The Grand Hotel York — Check In
stops.notes: Station Rise, YO1 6GD. Victorian railway hotel, right next to York station. Elegant rooms.

stops.name: Dinner — Guy Fawkes Inn
stops.notes: Historic pub on High Petergate, near York Minster. Named after the infamous conspirator who was born nearby. Atmospheric and central.

stops.name: York Ghost Walk
stops.notes: York is considered one of the most haunted cities in England. Evening walking tour through medieval streets and dark alleys. Book in advance online.

days.title: Day 5 — York Full Day
days.subtitle: August 8, 2026 · York Minster · National Railway Museum · Shambles Kitchen
days.tip: York is wonderfully walkable — most sights are within the city walls. Jorvik and York Castle Museum can get busy; arrive at opening. Castle Howard is a 30-minute drive and worth it.

stops.name: Morning Run — Scott Only
stops.notes: Solo morning run for Scott. York's city walls and riverside paths make great running routes — a loop along the walls and down to the River Ouse and back is about 3–4 miles. Rest of the group can sleep in.

stops.name: The Shambles
stops.notes: Medieval street with overhanging timber-framed buildings — said to have inspired Diagon Alley. Very atmospheric, now full of independent shops.

stops.name: York Minster
stops.notes: One of the largest Gothic cathedrals in Northern Europe. Stunning medieval stained glass. Climb the tower for city views. Allow 1–1.5 hours.

stops.name: Treasurer's House York
stops.notes: BOOKED — Order Ref: DBBPQQF5. 5 x adult tickets, £52.50 paid. Tour runs 11:15 AM–12:15 PM sharp — arrive by 11:05 AM to check in. Tours leave promptly. Magnificent furnished historic house with a famous ghost story — Roman soldiers reportedly march through the cellar. No large bags or pushchairs. No car park — walk from city centre.

stops.name: National Railway Museum
stops.notes: The world's largest railway museum and completely free. Mallard (the world's fastest steam locomotive), royal carriages, full-size locomotives, and fascinating railway history. About 15-minute walk west from Treasurer's House. Allow 1 hour. Grab lunch at the on-site Leeman Road Café — serves hot meals, sandwiches, cakes, and drinks. No need to leave the museum to eat.

stops.name: Jorvik Viking Centre
stops.notes: Ride through a recreation of 10th-century Viking York built on the actual excavation site. Fascinating, slightly kitsch, kids love it. Book online.

stops.name: York Castle Museum
stops.notes: Fascinating social history museum. Kirkgate — a reconstructed Victorian street — is the highlight. Dick Turpin was imprisoned in the original castle here.

stops.name: Clifford's Tower
stops.notes: BOOKED — Booking Ref: 45J87VEX. Paid £51.95. Show tickets at the welcome desk. Striking 13th-century royal keep perched on a mound — the last remaining part of York Castle. Panoramic views over the city from the top. Right next to York Castle Museum.

stops.name: Dinner — Star Inn The City
stops.notes: Riverside restaurant beside the Lendal Bridge. Modern Yorkshire cooking in a great setting. Reservation recommended.

stops.name: City Walls Walk
stops.notes: Walk along York's well-preserved Roman and medieval walls. Free, great views over the city rooftops. Partial circuit is fine.

stops.name: Bettys Cafe Tea Rooms
stops.notes: BOOKED — Table for 5, 8:30 PM. Confirmation #49448 (OpenTable). Evening dining menu — different from the daytime café menu. Pianist plays 6–9 PM. 6–8 St Helen's Square, York YO1 8QP. Cancellation policy: £20 per person for no-shows or cancellations within 24 hours.

days.title: Day 6 — Hadrian's Wall to Edinburgh
days.subtitle: August 9, 2026 · Housesteads Roman Fort · Alnwick Castle · Bamburgh Castle
days.tip: Check tide times for Lindisfarne before leaving — the causeway floods twice daily. Holy Island is only accessible for a few hours around low tide.

stops.name: Fuel Stop — York
stops.notes: Fill up and grab coffees before heading north.

stops.name: Housesteads Roman Fort
stops.notes: Best-preserved fort on Hadrian's Wall. Stunning ridge-top position with views across open moorland. Short uphill walk from the car park. Allow 1 hour.

stops.name: Alnwick Castle
stops.notes: Hogwarts exterior in the Harry Potter films. Still a working ducal castle. Dragon Quest trail, state rooms, broomstick training on the grounds. Allow 1–1.5 hours.

stops.name: Fuel Stop — Alnwick
stops.notes: Top up fuel in Alnwick before heading to the coast.

stops.name: Bamburgh Castle
stops.notes: Dramatic clifftop castle overlooking a pristine beach. One of England's most iconic views. The beach below is spectacular on a clear day.

stops.name: Lunch — Victoria Hotel
stops.notes: Pub lunch in Bamburgh village, convenient after the castle visit.

stops.name: Lindisfarne Priory (Holy Island)
stops.notes: CHECK TIDE TIMES before going. Causeway floods twice daily — only crossable ~3 hours either side of low tide. Medieval monastery ruin, peaceful and atmospheric. Book parking in advance.

stops.name: Drive to Edinburgh
stops.notes: ~1.5 hour drive north across the border. Welcome to Scotland.

stops.name: Hub by Premier Inn — Check In
stops.notes: Rose Street, EH2 2NN. Right in the heart of the New Town, perfect location.

stops.name: Dinner — The Last Drop
stops.notes: Historic pub on Grassmarket below Edinburgh Castle. Named for the public gallows that once stood here. Good atmosphere, Scottish food.

stops.name: Mary's Milk Bar
stops.notes: Grassmarket ice cream institution. Creative flavours, always a queue. A must-visit on any Edinburgh trip.

days.title: Day 7 — Rosslyn, Glenfinnan & Glencoe
days.subtitle: August 10, 2026 · Stirling Castle · quick bite (Tyndrum) · Glenfinnan Viaduct
days.tip: This is the big Highland drive day — start early. The Glenfinnan Viaduct viewpoint is a 20-minute walk uphill from the car park. Glencoe is best experienced on a walk into the valley, not just from the road.

stops.name: Stirling Castle
stops.notes: Opens ~9:30 AM. Royal Palace, Great Hall, views over the Forth Valley.

stops.name: Lunch — quick bite (Tyndrum)
stops.notes: Quick bite on the A82 heading northwest — keep it short to make the viaduct.

stops.name: Glenfinnan Viaduct
stops.notes: Westbound Jacobite steam train crosses ~1:20 PM — verify exact 2026 times.

stops.name: Glencoe
stops.notes: The Three Sisters — dark, brooding, unforgettable.

stops.name: Highland Cattle — Loch Lomond
stops.notes: Shaggy Highland cattle along Loch Lomond near Luss.

stops.name: Glasgow City Walk
stops.notes: Stroll the Merchant City / George Square.

stops.name: Dinner — Café Gandolfi
stops.notes: 64 Albion St, Merchant City.

stops.name: Hub by Premier Inn Edinburgh
stops.notes: Back to Edinburgh for the night.

days.title: Arthur's Seat Sunrise Hike, Edinburgh Castle & Royal Mile
days.subtitle: August 11, 2026 · Arthur's Seat · Edinburgh Castle · Royal Mile · Military Tattoo
days.tip: Book Edinburgh Castle and the Military Tattoo well in advance — both sell out in August. Arthur's Seat at dawn is truly magical. The Tattoo ends late; the walk back along the Royal Mile is festive.

stops.name: Arthur's Seat Sunrise Hike
stops.notes: Ancient volcanic peak rising above Edinburgh. 45-minute walk to the summit for panoramic views over the city, Forth, and Fife. Bring layers — it's windy at the top.

stops.name: Edinburgh Castle
stops.notes: Scotland's most visited attraction. Scottish Crown Jewels, Stone of Destiny, One O'Clock Gun, Great Hall. Perched on volcanic rock above the city. Book online well in advance. Allow 2 hours.

stops.name: Royal Mile
stops.notes: Mile-long medieval spine from Castle to Palace. During the Edinburgh Festival (Aug) the street is packed with performers and street food.

stops.name: Lunch — Edinburgh Larder
stops.notes: Scottish produce café on the Royal Mile. Known for excellent sandwiches, salads, and their famous haggis sausage roll.

stops.name: Palace of Holyroodhouse
stops.notes: The King's official Scottish residence. Mary Queen of Scots' chambers, the ruins of Holyrood Abbey. Book online. Allow 1.5 hours.

stops.name: Scottish National Museum
stops.notes: Free, world-class museum covering Scottish history, science, and culture. Dolly the Sheep, Lewis Chessmen, magnificent atrium.

stops.name: Dean Village
stops.notes: Hidden 800-year-old milling village in a wooded gorge, 10 minutes walk from Princes Street. Feels completely removed from the city above. Excellent photography.

stops.name: Mimi's Bakehouse
stops.notes: Wonderful bakery near Dean Village or the Royal Mile. Great cakes, scones, and coffee.

stops.name: Dinner — Deacon Brodie's Tavern
stops.notes: Historic pub on the Royal Mile, inspired by the real Deacon Brodie (inspiration for Jekyll and Hyde). Good Scottish pub food, great location.

stops.name: Victoria Street
stops.notes: Curved medieval street with colourful shopfronts — said to have inspired Diagon Alley. Browse the independent shops and galleries.

stops.name: Greyfriars Kirkyard
stops.notes: Historic kirkyard off Candlemaker Row — Greyfriars Bobby. Open access, 2 minutes from Victoria Street.

stops.name: Edinburgh Vaults Tour
stops.notes: Subterranean chambers beneath the South Bridge arches. Atmospheric and eerie. Book in advance.

stops.name: Royal Edinburgh Military Tattoo
stops.notes: World-famous annual event on the Castle Esplanade. Massed bands, Highland dancers, military displays from across the world. BOOKED — 5 tickets £702, Section 10, Row W. Spectacular finale with fireworks.

stops.name: Hub by Premier Inn
stops.notes: Rose Street, EH2 2NN.

days.title: Day 9 — Edinburgh to London via Ely
days.subtitle: August 12, 2026 · Almonry Kitchen, Ely · Ely Cathedral · King's College Chapel & The Backs
days.tip: The LNER East Coast Main Line is spectacular — grab window seats on the right side heading south for sea views near Berwick. Book the Ely lunch spot in advance if possible.

stops.name: LNER Train — Edinburgh to Ely
stops.notes: LNER service departing 07:30. Coach J, seats 43, 47, 44, 45, 46. Journey ~4 hours along the stunning East Coast Main Line.

stops.name: Lunch — Almonry Kitchen, Ely
stops.notes: Lovely café in the cathedral precincts. A civilised stop for lunch after the morning train.

stops.name: Ely Cathedral
stops.notes: The 'Ship of the Fens' — a magnificent Norman and Gothic cathedral rising dramatically from the flat fenland. Extraordinary octagonal Lantern tower. Allow 1 hour.

stops.name: Train — Ely to Cambridge
stops.notes: Short hop, ~15 minutes.

stops.name: King's College Chapel & The Backs
stops.notes: Glorious Gothic chapel on King's Parade. The Backs — the green lawns along the River Cam behind the colleges — are beautiful in summer. Punting available. Allow 1 hour.

stops.name: Train — Cambridge to London Kings Cross
stops.notes: ~55 minutes. Great Northern / LNER service.

stops.name: The LaLit London — Check In
stops.notes: 181 Tooley Street, SE1 2JR. Former grammar school building, now a luxurious boutique hotel. Near London Bridge.

stops.name: Dinner — Flat Iron Borough
stops.notes: Flat Iron steakhouse near Borough Market. Simple, excellent, affordable. No reservations — go early or queue.

stops.name: Dinner — Black and Blue Borough Market
South Bank Evening Walk
stops.notes: Stroll along the Thames Southbank — Tate Modern, Millennium Bridge, St Paul's across the water, Southbank Centre. Beautiful in the evening.

days.title: Day 10 — Canterbury & Dover
days.subtitle: August 13, 2026 · Borough Market · Canterbury Cathedral · Dover Castle
days.tip: Dojo app is required to join the Padella queue — download it in advance and get in the virtual queue at 4:30 PM sharp. Dover's Secret Wartime Tunnels need pre-booking.

stops.name: Borough Market
stops.notes: London's greatest food market. Open Thurs–Sat, packed on Saturday. Sample everything — cheesemakers, bakers, charcuterie, hot food. Just across from the hotel.

stops.name: Train — London Bridge to Canterbury
stops.notes: Southeastern train, ~1h 15min.

stops.name: Canterbury Cathedral
stops.notes: Mother church of the worldwide Anglican Communion. UNESCO World Heritage Site. Where Thomas Becket was murdered in 1170. Stunning medieval interior. Allow 1.5 hours.

stops.name: Canterbury City Walls Walk
stops.notes: Walk along the well-preserved medieval walls around the city. Good views and free.

stops.name: Lunch — Cathedral Lodge Cafe
stops.notes: Café within the Cathedral grounds. Convenient and pleasant setting.

stops.name: Train — Canterbury to Dover
stops.notes: ~25 minutes. Southeastern service.

stops.name: Dover Castle — Secret Wartime Tunnels
stops.notes: Clifftop castle above the White Cliffs. The underground tunnels used in WWII as a military HQ (Dunkirk evacuation was planned here) are extraordinary. Book in advance. Allow 2 hours.

stops.name: Train — Dover to London
stops.notes: ~1h 40min back to London.

stops.name: National Gallery
stops.notes: One of the world's great art collections — free entry. Trafalgar Square. Van Gogh's Sunflowers, Turner, da Vinci, Vermeer. Closes 6:00 PM on Thursdays.

stops.name: Dinner — Padella
stops.notes: Legendary handmade pasta restaurant at Borough Market. No reservations — use the Dojo app. Get in the virtual queue at 4:30 PM from anywhere. Pici cacio e pepe is unmissable.

stops.name: Borough Market Evening Walk
stops.notes: Evening stroll through Borough Market and along the Southbank. A great way to end the last full day.

stops.name: The LaLit London
stops.notes: 181 Tooley Street, SE1 2JR.

days.title: Day 11 — Fly Home
days.subtitle: August 14, 2026 · Tower Bridge Morning Walk
days.tip: The Thameslink at 10:10 AM gives a buffer but don't miss it — international check-in closes 90 minutes before departure. Have everything packed the night before.

stops.name: The Lalit London
stops.notes: Final hotel breakfast. Enjoy it — long day of travel ahead.

stops.name: Tower Bridge Morning Walk
stops.notes: Last look at the Thames and Tower Bridge before heading home. 5-minute walk from the hotel.

stops.name: The Lalit London
stops.notes: 181 Tooley Street, SE1 2JR. Check out with all bags.

stops.name: Flight Z0 783 — LGW to MCO
stops.notes: Norse Atlantic UK flight Z0 783. Departs 2:00 PM — HARD DEADLINE. ~9 hour flight home.
